definition: COSFIRE stands for Combination Of Shifted FIlter REsponses.
details: COSFIRE is a trainable filter, which can be used for interest point (keypoint) detection and pattern recognition in the field of computer vision.

explainer.lead: COSFIRE is a trainable computer-vision filter that combines filter responses taken at shifted positions. It can highlight interest points, also called keypoints, and help recognize visual patterns.

tiers.eli5: Imagine checking a picture with several small stencils, each placed a little distance from the others. COSFIRE looks at what those stencils find and combines the results to decide whether a particular pattern is present. It can be trained to look for useful points or patterns in pictures.
tiers.practitioner: Train the filter for the target keypoint or pattern, then evaluate and combine its shifted responses across image locations. The combined output can supply candidate keypoints or evidence for a pattern match. Check the output for unwanted responses to visually similar structures before using it downstream.
tiers.paperLevel: Let R(x) be a filter response at image location x, let delta_i be configured shifts, and let C be the combination operation. A plain-text abstraction is S(x) = C({R(x - delta_i)}), where S is the COSFIRE response. The filter is trainable and is used for interest-point detection and pattern recognition.

explainer.example: Suppose a COSFIRE filter has been trained for a particular keypoint. At image location x, it evaluates the filter responses, shifts each one by its configured offset, and combines them; a strong combined response makes x a candidate location for that keypoint.

usedIn.name: Interest-point detection
usedIn.detail: Produces candidate image keypoints from combined shifted filter responses.

usedIn.name: Pattern recognition
usedIn.detail: Uses a trained filter to identify target visual patterns.

explainer.intuition: A single response at one position may not capture the arrangement of a visual pattern. COSFIRE instead gathers responses from shifted relative positions and combines them into one response.
howItWorks: Train the filter for the target keypoint or visual pattern.
Evaluate filter responses at image locations.
Apply the configured shifts to those responses.
Combine the shifted responses into a COSFIRE response.
Use a strong response as a candidate keypoint or as evidence of the target pattern.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides one trainable filtering idea for two core computer-vision tasks: finding interest points and recognizing patterns. Its defining feature is the explicit combination of shifted responses rather than reliance on one unshifted response.
misconceptions: COSFIRE is a trainable filter, not a complete vision application by itself.
Its output is a combination of shifted responses, not just one raw filter response.
It is not limited to keypoint detection; it can also be used for pattern recognition.
